title: 10 Best Database Frontend Tools in 2026
summary: A database frontend turns tables into screens people can use. Ten tools for building one, grouped by what they build, and where each one stops.
body_markdown:
A database frontend is the interface that sits between people and a database: forms instead of` INSERT` statements, search instead of` WHERE` clauses, and permissions instead of shared credentials. Twenty years ago the answer was Microsoft Access. Today it is a web app, and you rarely need to write it from scratch. A new generation of tools connects to your existing database and builds the frontend for you.


Below are ten database frontend tools, grouped by what they build, with the point where each one stops.


## What a good database frontend does


- Connects to the database you already have, without migrating or copying data.
- Gives people tables, record pages, forms and dashboards rather than SQL.
- Validates what people enter before it reaches the database.
- Controls who sees and edits which tables, rows and fields.
- Can be changed as the process changes, ideally by the people who use it.


## The ten database frontend tools at a glance


Tool What it builds Databases Pricing model


Jet Admin Internal tools, portals, dashboards PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, Snowflake and 200+ sources Plan-based; unlimited users


Retool Developer-built internal tools Most SQL and NoSQL databases Per user


Appsmith Open source internal tools Most SQL and NoSQL databases Free open source; paid plans


Budibase Low-code CRUD apps Common SQL databases Free open source; paid plans


Softr Portals and apps from blocks Airtable, Google Sheets, some SQL Tiered plans


Directus Admin app and APIs Common SQL databases Source-available; paid cloud


NocoDB Spreadsheet-style frontend PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite and others Open source; paid cloud

Microsoft Power Apps Business apps in Microsoft 365 Dataverse, SQL Server, many connectors Per user


Microsoft Access Desktop database frontend Access, SQL Server via ODBC Included with some Microsoft 365 plans


## Internal tool builders


### 1. Jet Admin


Jet Admin connects to the database you already use and builds a frontend on it from a description: tables with search and filters, record pages that follow relationships, forms with validation, approval flows and dashboards. You refine it in a visual editor, or with custom React components, server-side functions and code synced to GitHub. Data stays in your database; Jet queries it in place.


It is built for frontends that many people use. Pricing is by AI credits with unlimited users on every plan, and roles can restrict rows and fields, so one frontend can serve support, finance and external partners with different views. Granular permissions, SSO and audit logs are on the Business plan and above; on-premise deployment is on Enterprise.


**Where it stops:** it builds business apps and portals, not public consumer websites or native mobile apps.


### 2. Retool


Retool is the best-known developer platform for internal tools, with a deep component library and strong database support.


**Where it stops:** it expects developers to build, and per-user pricing adds up as access widens.


### 3. Appsmith


Appsmith is an open source, self-hostable internal tool builder where developers bind widgets to queries with JavaScript.


**Where it stops:** non-developers struggle to maintain JavaScript-heavy apps.


### 4. Budibase


Budibase generates CRUD screens from database tables and adds automations, with open source self-hosting.


**Where it stops:** its component set limits more complex interfaces.


## Portal and app builders


### 5. Softr


Softr builds portals and simple apps from blocks, mainly on Airtable and Google Sheets, with some SQL support.


**Where it stops:** you are limited to its blocks, and SQL database support is narrower than dedicated tools.


### 6. WeWeb


WeWeb is a visual frontend builder for custom web apps, commonly paired with Supabase or Xano backends and REST APIs.


**Where it stops:** it expects a backend with an API; connecting directly to an arbitrary SQL database is not its model.


## Data platforms


### 7. Directus


Directus introspects your database and provides an admin app and REST and GraphQL APIs with permissions.


**Where it stops:** its app is generic data management, and it runs as a separate service with license conditions for larger companies.


### 8. NocoDB


NocoDB turns a database into a spreadsheet-style frontend with grid, form, kanban and gallery views.


**Where it stops:** spreadsheets suit editing, not multi-step processes.


## Microsoft options


### 9. Microsoft Power Apps


Power Apps builds business apps inside Microsoft 365 with connectors to Dataverse, SQL Server and many services.


**Where it stops:** it is most natural inside the Microsoft ecosystem, and premium connectors and per-user licensing raise the cost.


### 10. Microsoft Access


Access is still used as a desktop frontend, including on SQL Server through linked tables.


**Where it stops:** it is Windows desktop software, not a web app, and it does not suit remote or external users.


## Which database frontend to use


- **Many people need access with different permissions, and ops should shape it:** Jet Admin.
- **Developers will build internal tools in code:** Retool, Appsmith or Budibase.
- **You need a simple portal on Airtable or Sheets:** Softr.
- **You are building a custom web app on Supabase or Xano:** WeWeb.
- **You want instant APIs plus an admin:** Directus.
- **You want spreadsheet-style editing:** NocoDB.
- **You live in Microsoft 365:** Power Apps.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is a database frontend?


The user interface that lets people read and change data in a database through screens, forms and reports instead of queries.


### What is a modern alternative to Microsoft Access?


Web-based builders such as Jet Admin, Retool and Budibase provide forms, tables and reports on a server database, accessible from a browser with proper permissions.


### Can I build a database frontend without coding?


Yes. Tools such as Jet Admin generate the frontend from your schema and a description, and you adjust it visually.


## Start with the database you have


The best frontend is one built on your existing data, not a migration project.[Connect your database to Jet Admin](https://www.jetadmin.io/integrations) and give your team a frontend today.
